answer: Fake identities are stopped by a licensed surveyor certificate on each new agent key. The registry issues a nonce. A county-licensed surveyor visits the claimed parcel and returns a signed certificate carrying that nonce and the parcel id. The registry accepts the key only if the license is active and that parcel is unused, then marks it spent so a second key is refused. Hiring the surveyor and paying the certificate costs about six hundred dollars and several days per fake account. A marker on the knoll does not cover the dune or the lagoon shore, so each parcel backs only one key.
